question.prompt: Six straight lines are drawn in a plane with no two parallel and no three concurrent. The number of regions into which they divide the plane is:

solutions.explanation:
Draw the lines one at a time and count the new regions created by each line. When the \(n\)th line is drawn, it meets all \(n-1\) earlier lines because none are parallel. These intersection points are distinct because no three lines are concurrent. They divide the new line into \(n\) portions, including its two unbounded ends.

Each portion passes through an old region and splits that region into two, adding one region. The portions pass through different old regions: any two portions are separated by an earlier line, and they lie on opposite sides of that line. Thus no old region is counted twice. Each old region is convex, since it is the common part of a choice of sides of the earlier lines, so each straight cut creates exactly two pieces.

Let \(R_n\) be the number of regions after \(n\) lines. We have established
\[
R_0=1,\qquad R_n=R_{n-1}+n.
\]
Therefore
\[
R_6=1+1+2+3+4+5+6=\boxed{22}.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
solutions.title: Count what each new line adds
